findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote framed as a tabula ansata (dovetail handles either side), set against the 'Write to Mark' button in the hero
findings.fault: The button and the pull quote share one shape: a framed tablet with triangular handles. This page's one action and a static quote look alike, so the handles do not mean 'press me' or 'read me'. Once the layout round puts both on one screen, a reader will see a handled tablet and cannot tell if it is a button. The parts map marks the quote static, though it draws its own box.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor reading an article who has learned on the homepage that the handled tablet is how to contact Mark. They would either try the quote or stop trusting the handles as the contact cue. Angélique would also object, since every pull quote she adds would copy the button's shape.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Write to Mark' button (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com); the nav's CONTACT link
findings.fault: The page's one action is only a mailto link, and the address is not shown anywhere on the page. On a computer with no mail program set up (common on locked-down agency machines and webmail-only setups), clicking does nothing or opens an unwanted app, and there is no address the visitor can copy. CONTACT in the nav goes to '#', so there is no second route.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank using webmail on a managed work laptop. They click the one button, nothing useful happens, and they have no address to paste into their own mail.

findings.where: Hero name, the article headline and every Cinzel heading in minium red, against the minium-filled 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The colour reserved for the action is also the colour of every heading. The direction card says the one accent 'flows to the action', but here it goes mostly to headings. The largest red area on the first screen is the name, not the button, and an article page will have red headings and no action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for how to get in touch cannot follow the accent to the action, because red means 'heading' at least as often as 'act'. The layout round would inherit a colour that no longer marks the action.

findings.fault: This is a button (it replays the animation in place), but it looks like a link: underlined tracked capitals. It does not use the tile's own button look, the minium tablet. Underlining is the link's carrier, and here it marks an action, so the tile shows two looks for a button and gives a link's underline to an action.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that draw from this tile, and later visitors, who would meet underlined text that sometimes navigates and sometimes acts on the page.
